answer: Represent attestations as a weighted graph; propagate trust for at most t steps by random walks from anchored seeds. A Sybil set S with a small boundary-to-volume ratio has low conductance, so few walks enter it; its voting weight is bounded by seed mass reaching S plus at most t times the boundary-crossing flow. A spiral of internal attestations cannot create external trust: isolation is the nadir of exposure, while a grove of independent honest anchors raises the cut flow and limits capture.
